summary: The note explains cross-training, the practice of doing exercise outside one's primary sport, and argues it reduces injury risk and improves strength, endurance and agility. It gives sport-specific recommendations for runners, cyclists, swimmers and team-sport athletes, with quotes from local coaches and trainers. It also covers building a plan, monitoring progress, and how local clubs promote cross-training, in the context of local health initiatives since September 2023.
one_line: Cross-training reduces injury risk and boosts performance, with sport-specific examples and local expert advice on planning, monitoring and community promotion.
key_facts: Cross-training means engaging in forms of exercise beyond an individual's primary sport, such as a distance runner adding cycling or swimming.
Local health and wellness initiatives have highlighted cross-training since September 2023.
Dr. Linda Park, a sports medicine expert, says varied workouts can prevent overuse injuries that stem from repetitive strain on specific muscle groups.
Cross-training can also prevent workout boredom and help people stick with exercise programs long-term.
For runners, low-impact cycling and swimming maintain cardiovascular fitness while giving joints a break; swimming can increase lung capacity and cycling builds quadriceps and hamstrings.
Marathon coach Michael Thompson said on October 15, 2023 that many of his athletes improved running times after adding regular cycling sessions.
Cyclists are advised to add weight training for the upper body and Pilates for core stability and posture; Jessica Sanders reported better core strength after adding Pilates in late September.
Swimmers benefit from yoga for flexibility and core strength and from running for bone density, since swimming is not weight-bearing; collegiate swimmer Annie Kim added two days of yoga weekly.
Team-sport athletes in soccer, basketball and football benefit from aerobic and anaerobic exercise, plyometrics, agility ladders, cone drills and resistance training.
Soccer coach Roberto Garcia said at a November 3, 2023 workshop that agility drills boost foot speed and mental acuity for quicker decisions.
Emily Scott designs plans by identifying what is missing from a client's regimen, such as cardio, strength training or flexibility, and rest and recovery should be included to avoid overtraining.
James Carter launched a monthly cross-training workshop for local athletes starting October 2023 and tracks resting heart rates and performance stats, adjusting plans if there is a plateau or dip.
Rachel Lee, operations manager at the Downtown Fitness Club, says runners joining dance fitness classes or swimmers lifting weights is becoming the norm.
